I am a woman of 41 years here in Mtwara, and I farm my 1.30 hectares of maize on land that belongs to my household. Chemical fertilizer is expensive and the shops are far, so I cannot afford it this season — instead I will spread the manure from my few goats and chickens on the field. I will plant the local maize seeds I saved from last harvest because they know our soil and the rains here, and I depend on the rain because I have no way to irrigate. My children and I will do most of the work ourselves, but at weeding time and harvest I will pay a few neighbors to help me finish on time.
